page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server configured with an AMD EPYC 9575F processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 20 vCPUs mapped to 20 physical cores with shared CPU allocation running at 2.0 GHz. The system features 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding 12.8 GB of RAM per core. Graphics and parallel computing acceleration are handled by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 48 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, this server demonstrates top-tier single-core and multi-core performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2931.0 and a multi-core score of 24099.0. Cryptographic and vector execution capabilities are supported by hardware flags including AVX-512 and AES. Memory bandwidth is strong, reaching 3960.24 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 309.72 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For machine learning workloads, the NVIDIA L40S GPU delivers top-tier LLM inference speeds on small models, processing 4434.62 tokens/sec for prompts, while maintaining strong performance on medium 7B models with 36.85 tokens/sec for text generation. Large 70B model inference falls into the average tier, processing prompts at 14.75 tokens/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers a qualitative balance of high-capacity system memory and dedicated GPU VRAM, making it efficient for memory-intensive parallel processing without requiring multi-GPU overhead. However, the lack of bundled local storage requires external volume attachments, which may introduce I/O latency tradeoffs. The shared CPU allocation is another consideration for sustained, non-GPU CPU-bound workloads. This configuration is highly suited for deep learning inference, image processing, ray tracing, and data science workloads requiring substantial memory and GPU acceleration.
